description: Develops foundational probability theory and classical statistical inference methodologies required for rigorous data analysis, machine learning models, and stochastic modeling.
learning_objectives: Understand probability axioms, conditional probability, Bayes theorem, and random variable distributions.
Compute moments, expectations, variances, joint distributions, and conditional expectations.
Apply asymptotic limit theorems including Chebyshev inequality, WLLN, and the Central Limit Theorem.
Perform point and interval estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and hypothesis testing.
outline: Probability Foundations: Sample spaces, events, conditional probability, Bayes rule, law of total probability, independence.
Random Variables: Discrete and continuous random variables, PMF, PDF, CDF, expectation, variance, moments, moment generating functions.
Joint & Conditional Distributions: Multiple random variables, joint and marginal distributions, covariance, correlation, conditional expectation.
Inequalities & Limit Theorems: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities, convergence in probability and distribution, Weak Law of Large Numbers, Central Limit Theorem.
Statistical Estimation: Unbiasedness, consistency, sufficiency, efficiency, Method of Moments, Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE).
Hypothesis Testing: Null/alternative hypotheses, Type I/II errors, p-values, Neyman-Pearson lemma, likelihood ratio tests, confidence intervals.
Lab Component: Statistical computing, probability simulations, and data modeling in Python/R.
